blocks.text: Many developers prefer a clean screen while writing code. Having the mouse cursor hover over your text can be a distraction. Since VS Code does not follow the system-level hide cursor settings found in macOS, you need to manage this within the editor itself.
Installing the Cursor Auto Hide extension

The most effective way to manage your mouse cursor visibility is through a community extension. The Cursor Auto Hide extension is the standard choice for this task. It monitors your typing and hides the mouse pointer after a set period of inactivity.
How to customize your text insertion cursor

If you do not want to hide the mouse cursor but find the text insertion caret distracting, you can change its appearance. VS Code offers several styles, including block, line, and underline. You can also stop the blinking animation to keep the editor steady.

blocks.text: Managing settings through the Command Palette

The fastest way to reach these settings is the Command Palette. Press Command + Shift + P to open it. Type 'Open User Settings (JSON)' to edit your configuration file directly. This method allows you to apply changes quickly without navigating through multiple menus.
Common issues and how to fix them

When you install extensions that modify the workbench, you might see a warning about a corrupt installation. This is normal for extensions that patch the UI. You can dismiss this warning by clicking the gear icon on the notification and selecting 'Don't Show Again'.

faq.question: Can I hide the mouse cursor without an extension?
faq.answer: No, VS Code does not provide a native setting to hide the mouse cursor while typing.

faq.question: Is the Cursor Auto Hide extension safe?
faq.answer: Yes, it is a widely used extension. The warning message you might see is a common side effect of how it interacts with the VS Code workbench.
